MATHEMATICS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #1
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Every product in the 5 times table ends in (1 mark)
   A. 5 or 9
   B. 2 or 7
   C. 0 or 5
   D. 1 or 6

2. How many lines of symmetry does a triangle with three equal sides have? (1 mark)
   A. 1
   B. 4
   C. 3
   D. 2

3. On an analogue clock the short hour hand has reached or passed the number 7 but not yet reached the next number, and the long minute hand points to the number 9. What time is shown? (1 mark)
   A. 7:09
   B. 7:15
   C. 8:45
   D. 7:45

4. A shopping list has three items costing Ksh 6,500, Ksh 1,750 and Ksh 850. What is the total cost? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 9,110
   B. Ksh 9,000
   C. Ksh 9,200
   D. Ksh 9,100

5. What number is the Roman numeral X? (1 mark)
   A. 3
   B. 1
   C. 2
   D. 10

6. Cuboid A is 5 by 2 by 4 blocks (length, width, height). Cuboid B is 4 by 4 by 2 blocks. Which has the greater volume? (1 mark)
   A. They are equal
   B. Cuboid B
   C. Cuboid A
   D. It cannot be told

7. Which expression shows "n subtracted from 20"? (1 mark)
   A. n − 20
   B. 20 + n
   C. 20 − n
   D. 20n

8. What is 96 ÷ 3? (1 mark)
   A. 42
   B. 31
   C. 33
   D. 32

9. One unit costs Ksh 120. What is the cost of 2 packets of maize flour? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 120
   B. Ksh 250
   C. Ksh 240
   D. Ksh 122

10. How many times do you need to regroup when you add 1,234 + 4,321? (1 mark)
   A. 2
   B. 3
   C. 0
   D. 1

11. Estimate 24 × 18 by rounding each number to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 4,000
   B. 300
   C. 400
   D. 500

12. Which list shows all the factors of 42? (1 mark)
   A. 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 14, 21
   B. 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 14, 21, 42
   C. 1, 2, 6, 7, 14, 21, 42
   D. 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 14, 21, 42

13. Work out 4,250 − 1,875. (1 mark)
   A. 2,375
   B. 3,625
   C. 2,385
   D. 2,275

14. The table shows the favourite fruits of 10 pupils: mango 4, banana 3, orange 2, pawpaw 1. How many are NOT pawpaw? (1 mark)
   A. 1
   B. 10
   C. 11
   D. 9

15. What is raw data? (1 mark)
   A. A picture of data
   B. Data written in a table
   C. Data that has been collected but not yet arranged
   D. Data that is wrong

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. A rectangular field is 45 m long and 30 m wide. (a) Find its perimeter. (b) A farmer wants to fence it but leaves two gates of 3 m each. How many metres of fence does he need? (5 marks)

17. A tailor has 3 m 60 cm of cloth and uses 1 m 85 cm. How much cloth is left? (3 marks)

18. Divide 84 by 4 and check your answer. (3 marks)

19. A farmer had 6,500 seedlings and planted 2,875. How many were left? Estimate first by rounding to the nearest ten. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #1 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — 0 or 5
   5, 10, 15, 20, 25 ... All end in 0 or 5.

2. C — 3
   Each line goes from a corner to the middle of the opposite side.

3. D — 7:45
   Each number on the clock face is worth 5 minutes. The minute hand at 9 shows 9 × 5 = 45 minutes, so the time is 7:45.

4. D — Ksh 9,100
   Add the three costs: 6,500 + 1,750 + 850 = 9,100.

5. D — 10
   X stands for 10.

6. C — Cuboid A
   A = 5 × 2 × 4 = 40 blocks. B = 4 × 4 × 2 = 32 blocks. Cuboid A is greater.

7. C — 20 − n
   The key words tell us the operation. "n subtracted from 20" is written 20 − n.

8. D — 32
   3 × 32 = 96, so 96 ÷ 3 = 32.

9. C — Ksh 240
   Cost = number × price = 2 × 120 = Ksh 240.

10. C — 0
   Check each column from the right for a total of 10 or more, remembering the carried digit. 1,234 + 4,321 needs 0 regroupings.

11. C — 400
   24 rounds to 20 and 18 rounds to 20. 20 × 20 = 400.

12. B — 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 14, 21, 42
   Pair up numbers that multiply to 42. The factors are 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 14, 21, 42.

13. A — 2,375
   Subtract from the ones, regrouping when the top digit is smaller. 4,250 − 1,875 = 2,375. Check: 2,375 + 1,875 = 4,250.

14. D — 9
   10 − 1 = 9.

15. C — Data that has been collected but not yet arranged
   Raw data is untidy information straight from collection.

SECTION B
----
16. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) 150 m (b) 144 m
   Working / marking points: (a) 45 + 30 + 45 + 30 = 150 m (2 marks for method, 1 mark for the answer with unit); (b) 2 × 3 = 6 m and 150 − 6 = 144 m (2 marks total, awarded 1 for 6 m and 1 for 144 m). Total 5 marks.

17. (3 marks)
   Answer: 1 m 75 cm
   Working / marking points: 360 − 185 = 175 cm (2 marks); 175 cm = 1 m 75 cm (1 mark).

18. (3 marks)
   Answer: 21
   Working / marking points: 80 ÷ 4 = 20 (1 mark); 4 ÷ 4 = 1, so 21 (1 mark); check 21 × 4 = 84 (1 mark).

19. (4 marks)
   Answer: Estimate 6,500 − 2,880 = 3,620. Exact: 3,625 seedlings.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for rounding 2,875 to 2,880 (6,500 stays), 1 mark for the estimate, 1 mark for the exact working, 1 mark for the answer.
